chapter_theme: The fourth stretch of Pattinathar's garland to the Fullness (பூரணம்) turns from the question 'how did you become each thing' to the disputants and to the poet himself. Those who name you sky, cosmos, light, breath, silence, the Supreme, the sun or the five letters do not know themselves, your name, your way or the order of the letters; the poet confesses that lust, women, the body taken for a support, maya's stupor and puja mixed with worldly enjoyment cost him his understanding; and then he turns the complaint on the Fullness itself, which created and destroys, which divided night from day, sin from merit, heaven from hell, calm from anger, caste from caste, and which stands as bond, soul and Lord at once. The run closes on union: I am you and you are I, and when the two are one you do not cloy, like honey.
structure_note: Four groups: 749 to 754, the rival accounts of the Fullness and what their speakers do not know, with 753 as the poet's own admission that he cannot find the one thing under all of them; 755 to 764, confession in the first person, each verse ending in a verb of loss (பயனழிந்தேன், பிறந்திறந்தேன், கலங்கினேன், தட்டழிந்தேன், அறிவழிந்தேன்); 765 to 771, the Fullness as the maker of every division, each ending in அறியேன் or படைத்தனையே; 772 and 773, the plea and the union. The refrain பூரணமே closes every couplet and is the addressee, not the subject, of each.

749.reading: Those who call you sky, those who call you the cosmic egg, who speak knowledge with the mouth alone and say 'it is I': idle talkers, they do not know themselves.
749.nuance: வாய்ஞானம், mouth-knowledge, is the charge; தானென்பார் may be those who say 'I am it' (the Vedantin's claim) or those who speak only of themselves, and either way தனையறியார் answers it: the one who says 'I' has not known the 'I'. The verse opens a run (749 to 752) in which each line's என்பார் names a school.

750.reading: Those who say 'the beginning', those who say 'the end', those who say 'the light standing between the two': they do not know the work of nada.
750.nuance: நாதத்தொழில், the work of nada, is the coded term. Tradition takes nada as the first stir of sound from which the world unfolds, and in yoga as the inner sound heard when the breath is stilled; the verse may mean that the schools of beginning, end and middle light have not heard the sound, or have not understood how sound makes the world. The verse does not decide.

751.reading: Those who say 'breath', those who say 'the heart', those who say 'the release called silence', those who say 'speech': they do not know your name.
751.nuance: Four methods are named and set aside together: the breath (the Siddhars' own vaasi practice), the mind, silence taken as release, and speech (mantra and recitation). Silence is placed among the sayings, so even மோனம் is here something people 'say'. What they lack is உன்னுடைய பேர், your name, which the poem never supplies beyond the refrain.

752.reading: Those who say 'the Supreme', those who say 'the sun', those who say 'the boon that stands as the void expanse': they do not know your way.
752.nuance: பானு, the sun, can be the sun of the sky or, in the Siddhars' cipher, the right-hand breath; the plain list of schools (Vedanta's param, a sun cult, the teaching of the void) stands without the cipher. பாழ்வெளி, the void expanse, is a term the Siddhars use for the goal itself, and the verse counts even that as a saying that misses the way.

753.reading: However many people have taken you up and told you in their own words, I cannot discern the one thing that is common to all of them.
753.nuance: The verse closes the list of 749 to 752 with the poet's own admission: he does not claim a better account, only that the one thing under the many accounts (அத்தனை பேர்க்கு ஒன்றானது) escapes him. அரிகிலேன் is 'I do not know' (அறிகிலேன்), spelled with the alveolar.

754.reading: Those who say 'na and ma', those who say 'si in the middle', those who say 'va and ya': they do not know the order of the kinds.
754.nuance: The letters are those of நமசிவாய in sequence, with சி placed at the centre (நடுவே சிகாரம்). வகை, the kinds or arrangement, is what the reciters miss: the Tirumanthiram teaches orders of the five letters, and tradition reads 'knowing the order' as knowing what each letter stands for (Lord, soul, grace, bond, concealment). The verse keeps the mantra and faults the reciters, as Sivavakkiyar does.

755.reading: Sunk in the stupor of lust as though it were something great, unable to tell one thing from another, I threw away what life was for.
755.nuance: மகத்துவமாய் qualifies the poet's own state: lust held as a greatness, or the poet puffed up inside it. பகுத்தறிதல், discrimination, is the faculty named as lost, and the loss is of பயன், the fruit or use of the birth.

756.reading: Not gazing with love on the true substance, I was born and died again through infatuation with women.
756.nuance: பிறந்திறந்தேன் is a single compound verb, born-and-died, so the births are many and the cause is one. உண்மைப்பொருள், the true substance, is what the Fullness is called when it is an object of sight rather than of speech.

757.reading: Not praising you with a full mouth and rejoicing in you, I took a body and was thrown into confusion.
757.nuance: காயமெடுத்து, taking a body, is the cause of the confusion as well as its setting; the only remedy named is praise, the devotional act the poet's own Puranamalai performs. வோற்றாமல் is a spelling of போற்றாமல்.

758.reading: As a cloud hides the moon, so I, caught in bondage, do not see you.
758.nuance: The moon is not dimmed by the cloud; the figure puts the obstacle in the seer and leaves the Fullness unchanged. பந்தம், the bond, is the cloud, and the verse does not say what the bond is made of.

759.reading: Not praising the red lotus feet day after day, I stood without support and wandered here.
759.nuance: அந்தரமாய், in mid-air, is to stand on nothing; the feet are the support the poet failed to take, and அலைந்தேன் (I wandered) is the verb of 774, where the wandering is placed in a void.

760.reading: Taking this body, as unstable as a bubble on water, for my support, I was ruined.
760.nuance: தாரகம், the support or saviour, is the word for what carries one across; the error is not having a body but resting one's weight on it. The bubble on water is the common Tamil figure for the body's impermanence.

761.reading: Thinking of you with a melting heart and praising you, I still do not know how to drive out the long deceit.
761.nuance: நெடு வஞ்சகம், the long deceit, is not assigned an owner: the world's deceit, maya's, or the poet's own. The verse grants that the melting and the praise have happened and says they have not been enough, which separates it from the confessions around it.

762.reading: Not knowing in my heart that you stood filling everything like the oil in a sesame seed, I melted away.
762.nuance: Oil in sesame is the stock figure for a pervasion that cannot be seen from outside and is found only by pressing. உருகினேன் can be the melting of devotion or the wasting of grief; after அறியாது (not knowing) the second fits, and the melting is in vain because its object was already within.

763.reading: Fallen into the stupor of the world that is maya, I did not put an end to unceasing birth.
763.nuance: மாயாப்பிரபஞ்சம் makes the world and maya one compound, and ஓயாச்சனனம், birth that does not rest, is its product. The verse states the Saiva goal, ending birth, as the thing left undone.

764.reading: Through enjoyment, the puja and the pleasures of the world together, I grew greedy and lost my understanding.
764.nuance: Puja is set beside புவனபோகம், worldly enjoyment, under one word for enjoyment (போக்கியம்). This can mean puja performed for the sake of enjoyment, or that ritual worship was itself one more thing the poet enjoyed; on either reading worship is counted among what cost him his understanding, not among the remedies.

765.reading: You create and you destroy; and if you so much as look, you wipe out the letters Brahma wrote and make one shine as a deathless being.
765.nuance: பிரமாவெழுத்து is Brahma's writing on the skull, fate; தொடைத்து (wiping it off) sets the Fullness above fate. சிரஞ்சீவி, the long-lived or deathless, is read by the Siddhars as the body kept from death and by others as release from rebirth; the verse supports both, since what is wiped out is the written span of a life.

766.reading: Is it even fitting that I should know the device by which you stood as mantra, as sastra and as the four Vedas?
766.nuance: தந்திரம் is the device or art, and also the Tantra as a class of text beside mantra and sastra; the verse can list four kinds of scripture as forms of the Fullness, or ask after the trick by which the formless became text. தகுமோ, 'is it fitting', makes the ignorance a matter of standing rather than of effort.

767.reading: I do not know the connection by which you divided yourself into night, into day, and into the word called 'perpetual time'.
767.nuance: அனவரத காலம் is unending time, and it is named as a சொல், a word: the divisions of time are divisions in language. தொடர்பு, the connection, is what joins the undivided to its partitions, and the verse leaves it unknown.

768.reading: Though there are the two one goes to, hell and heaven, I do not understand what it is to say 'Hara, Hara'.
768.nuance: The verse grants the two destinations and sets against them the cry of the name, அரகரா, which belongs to neither. The point is left implicit: the name is what one says who is bound for neither place, and the poet cannot yet say it with understanding.

769.reading: By the division called sin and merit you create and destroy, and you planted longing here; the grace in that I do not understand.
769.nuance: ஆவல், longing, is set here by the Fullness itself, and the verse calls the arrangement அருள், grace, while confessing that it cannot see the grace in it. The Siddhanta position that the Lord gives the soul its deeds and their fruits as a help toward release is here stated from the side of the soul that does not feel helped.

770.reading: Calm and anger, the differences of caste, kinship and the intellect: all these you yourself created.
770.nuance: சாதி பேதங்கள், the differences of caste, are listed between anger and intellect as one more pair of the created world. பாந்தம் is read as பந்தம், the tie of kin or the bond; a reading as friendship (பாந்தவம்) also stands. The list makes caste real and made, not natural, which is both more and less than Sivavakkiyar's denial of it.

771.reading: As the bond you stood as the body, as the soul you stood as life, and in love you yourself stood as the substance.
771.nuance: The three categories of Saiva Siddhanta, pasam, pasu and pati, are mapped on to body, life and the Lord, and all three are said of the one Fullness in the second person. This folds the Siddhanta triad into a single being, which Siddhanta itself does not do; the word பொருள் for the third term, with நேசமுடன், keeps the Lord's place as the substance and the lover.

772.reading: Take pity on your devotees who have nothing, come into this world, and grant in grace that we bow low at your feet.
772.nuance: ஏதிலடியார் can be devotees without anything, or devotees who are strangers, without kin or standing; the plea is for the Fullness to come இகத்தில், into this world, which treats the pervading one as also absent. The couplet is the only direct petition in the chapter.

773.reading: I am you and you are I; when the two become one, you do not cloy, like the taste of honey.
773.nuance: தெவிட்டாய், 'you do not cloy', makes the union a taste that does not tire the tongue, so the bliss is continuing rather than momentary. The formula நானே நீ நீயே நான் is the Vedantic identity stated in the second person to a God; the verse keeps the two pronouns while claiming their oneness.

links.note: Sivavakkiyar tells the devotees who keep saying 'the five letters and the three' that the thing is neither, and sends them to press the five into the heart and find the one letter; Pattinathar lists the same five by their syllables and says the reciters do not know the order of the kinds. Both keep the mantra and fault the recitation that stops at the letters.

The Naladiyar praises those firm in understanding who see the body as a bubble in pelting rain and resolve to end their wandering; Pattinathar confesses the opposite history, having taken the bubble for his support. The verdict on the body is the same and the Naladiyar's praised man is what the poet failed to be.

Tirumular's body is a bubble on flowing water, a shadow-man, camphor in flame, and it goes into the Supreme; Pattinathar's bubble body is what he mistook for a தாரகம், a support. In Tirumular the bubble's dissolving is the return to the Supreme; in Pattinathar it is the collapse of a false foundation.

Sivavakkiyar: like oil in a sesame seed our Lord is everywhere and within you, yet you fools swing to and fro. Pattinathar turns the same figure on himself: not knowing the oil was in the seed, he melted. The image makes the pervasion invisible until pressed for, and both poets make the failure to know it the fault.

Tirumular says the Lord set hell and heaven and endless births for souls by grace, and that those who cannot see what is separate are the souls that took on karma; Pattinathar says the Fullness creates and destroys by the division of sin and merit and plants longing, and calls this grace he cannot understand. Both make the moral machinery the Lord's gift; Tirumular explains it and Pattinathar leaves it unexplained.

Sivavakkiyar asks what caste is, since all water is one water and the five elements are one; Pattinathar says the differences of caste were created by the Fullness, in the same breath as calm, anger, kinship and intellect. Pattinathar does not deny the distinctions but files them among the made and transient; Sivavakkiyar denies that they are anything. Both deny them weight, by different routes.

Agasthiyar says body, life and pooranam are one, though a few in the world call them different, and that body and life are pooranam's foot and head; Pattinathar says the Fullness stood as the body in the role of bond, as life in the role of soul, and as the substance itself. Both make the Siddhanta triad three names for one Fullness.

Tirumular keeps pati, pasu and pasam as three beginningless realities, of which pasu and pasam cannot reach pati and do not remain when he draws near; Pattinathar addresses all three, bond, soul and substance, as the one Fullness standing in three ways. On the Siddhanta reading of 115, in which the three are distinct and the bond is never the Lord, Pattinathar's identification of the bond with the Fullness is incompatible with it; on a monist reading of 115's last line, the two agree that only pati remains.

Tirumular: nearing him, there is no difference such as I and you, and humans revel in bliss as in honey. Pattinathar: I am you, you are I, and when the two are one you do not cloy, like honey. The claim and the figure coincide; Pattinathar adds that the honey does not tire the tongue.

Arunagirinathar names the release in which 'I am you and you are I' (நானே நீயாய் நீயே நானாய்) as what the Vedas cannot search out and asks whether he will die without it; Pattinathar says the same four words to the Fullness as something reached. The one formula is the unreached goal in the Thiruppugazh and the attained union here.

Tirumular's samadhi gives the unceasing honey of Siva's bliss which those who drink it do not leave; Pattinathar's union is a honey that does not cloy. Both answer the same doubt about bliss, that it might sate or end, with the honey that keeps its taste.

source_issues: 757 line 1 prints வோற்றாமல் for போற்றாமல்; 753 line 2 prints அரிகிலேன் for அறிகிலேன் (alveolar for retroflex, a common 1887 spelling).
The work is printed without word spaces throughout 749 to 773, so some splits (மகத்துவமாய், பாந்தமென்றும்) rest on the reader.
